correctness.rationale: Independent recomputation confirms all essential inferences of the DOWNGRADED one-sided claim (not the registered exact-maximum claim). G* adjacency (18x18) has all degrees 3, 27 edges exactly matching DRAFT edge list, BFS covers 18 vertices, C(18,3) triple scan finds zero triangles. numpy eigvalsh recomputed spectrum matches stored eig to <1e-12; lmin=-2.7898586072688976, h=1+3/(-lmin)=2.0753233128673925 matches claim. Primal X (18x18, symmetric to 0) has zero support violations on all i!=j nonedges of G* (<1e-9), trace 0.9999999999999999, min eigenvalue -2.36e-17 (>= -1e-9 threshold), sum 2.1960839211692655 matching theta_lb; hence theta(complement)>=2.19608 is a valid primal lower bound under the fixed convention (zeros on nonedges of G = edges of complement, tr=1, PSD). Gap 2.1960839211692655-2.0753233128673925=0.1207606083018731 >=0.1207606083 and >=0.12 margin both hold. Exact alpha=8 confirmed twice: independent branch-and-bound returns 8, exhaustive C(18,9)=48620 scan finds no independent 9-set, and witness set {0,2,6,7,8,10,14,15} (alpha_set 50629) is independent. DRAFT honestly discloses full-stratum D* NOT determined, theta upper bound heuristic only, numpy double precision, 1e-9 tolerances. Non-essential defect: stated sandwich 'h <= theta_LB <= alpha' as a general consistency check is theoretically mis-framed (theta(complement) is bounded by omega(G)<=theta<=chi(G), not by alpha(G); h vs theta ordering is a comparison theorem, not a sandwich with alpha). Numerically 2.0753<=2.1961<=8 holds here so no false numeric claim, and main gap inference does not depend on it. Proof vs evidence correctly distinguished: h/alpha/graph properties are exact replay; theta LB is certified feasible point; theta UB (~2.35) and 11-graph brackets correctly labeled heuristic, not proof.

originality.rationale: Delivered result is materially narrower than the admitted target and is not substantively new. Admitted target: exact maximum D*=max|theta(comp)-(1+3/(-lmin))| over the COMPLETE connected triangle-free cubic n=18 stratum with maximality certificate and distributions. Delivered: one-sided lower bound D*>=0.1207606083 from a single config-model seed (RTF_seed77) via one primal-feasible X, plus an 11-graph explicitly incomplete pool. Existence of a strict theta-vs-Hoffman gap is already established general theory, not a new per-stratum extremal: de Carli Silva et al. (2106.11121) proves Hoffman-sum vs theta comparison framework (Hoffman-sum at least as good as theta, i.e. the two bounds are distinct and comparable, with strict cases); Elphick-Wocjan (1210.7844) gives unified spectral chi-bounds with examples outperforming/differing from each other. That a random 18-vertex triangle-free cubic has theta(comp)-h ~0.07-0.31 is shown by the candidate's own 11-graph table (dual UB gaps 0.07-0.31), proving the witness is generic, not distinguished. The specific number 0.1207 is a solver-dependent primal feasible value (true theta lies somewhere in [2.196,2.353] per their UB), not a canonical extremal value; no maximality scan, no distribution, no lexicographically-smallest extremal. A timestamp or failed in-lane search does not establish priority. Hence no prior per-stratum maximum is beaten because none is computed, and the single-instance strictness was already implied by known separation of the two chi lower bounds.

value.rationale: Even taking correctness as given, the downgraded single-witness lower bound is not independently worth finding later. It is an arbitrary-slice anecdote: one random seed's primal objective minus Hoffman value, with true theta unknown (heuristic interval width ~0.16 exceeds the claimed gap 0.12). No complete-stratum enumeration (41301 pool not generated, triangle-free count not determined), no h/theta/alpha distributions or extrema, no dual brackets to <1e-4 proving maximality, so neither the primary exact-D* claim nor the predefined fallback citable benchmark (counts, distributions, slack extrema, witnessed extremals with certificates and replay over the full stratum) is delivered. The 11-graph table is explicitly a demonstration pool, not a census. Downstream calibration/benchmark use claimed in topic.json requires completeness and maximality; a generic ~0.1 gap reproducible on almost any random triangle-free cubic (per candidate's own table) has no such use. This falls under tiny unmotivated gain / arbitrary parameter instance / unexplained enumeration: correct but not retrievable-value science.
